svg.title: Tensile stress versus strain for a mammalian tendon
svg.desc: Tensile stress increases gradually with strain in the toe region, then proportionally in the linear region. In the failure region the stress peaks and falls as fibers tear. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Why a tendon’s stress–strain curve starts soft
Failure region: fibers tear one by one
Schematic, not calibrated: wavy collagen fibers straighten with little force, then stretch
elastically, then fail. Extension is exaggerated.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
